edits.text: Keep a finite copula or main verb (including auxiliaries) together with its immediately following obligatory complement — a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, numeral+unit, or clause — when there is no intervening punctuation; prefer placing a cut after that complement rather than between verb and complement.
- Keep a numeral or explicit quantity (digits or spelled-out) together with the immediately following unit or the noun it quantifies (years, kilometers, barrels, people, etc.).

Fallback ordering: prefer a cut that keeps a finite verb or auxiliary together with its immediately following obligatory complement (noun phrase, prepositional phrase, numeral+unit, or clause) over a cut that falls immediately after punctuation or a clear clause boundary; if neither applies, prefer a cut that keeps a numeral or explicit quantity together with its immediately following unit/noun over one that splits them.

Fallback ordering: prefer a cut that keeps a numeral or explicit quantity together with its immediately following unit or the noun it quantifies; prefer a cut immediately before the numeral or immediately after the unit over a cut placed between the numeral and its unit.
